title: Worksheet 4: For Loop vs. While Loop
directions: Read the paragraph below carefully. Then answer all questions using ONLY the information in the paragraph. Circle the letter of the best answer.
paragraph: Although for loops and while loops can sometimes be used to accomplish similar tasks, choosing the right one often depends on whether the number of repetitions needed is known in advance. A for loop is generally the clearer, more natural choice when a programmer already knows exactly how many times a task needs to repeat before the loop even begins running, such as processing every item in a list containing exactly 15 entries. A while loop, on the other hand, is generally a better fit when the number of repetitions cannot be known in advance, because it depends on something that happens while the program is actually running, such as a game continuing to run until a player's health reaches zero, or a program continuing to ask for input until the user finally enters a valid response. It is technically possible to rewrite almost any for loop as a while loop, and almost any while loop as a for loop, but doing so often makes the code harder to read, since each loop type is generally designed to clearly signal, at a glance, what kind of repetition a programmer originally intended.

questions.correct: Whether the number of repetitions needed is known in advance

questions.text: A programmer is writing a program that must continue running a game until a player's health reaches zero, but the exact number of turns that will take cannot be known before the game starts. Based on the paragraph's guidance about when each loop type generally fits best, which loop type is the better natural fit for this situation?
questions.correct: A while loop, since the number of repetitions depends on something that happens while the program runs
distractors: Neither loop type could be used for this situation at all
A for loop, since the number of turns is always known in advance
A for loop, since the paragraph says for loops are always the better choice for games

questions.correct: The number of repetitions would stay the same, but the code would likely become harder to read, since it wouldn't clearly signal the loop's original intent
